item.title: Michael Jackson Holds U.K. Albums Chart Crown as Compilation Scores Second Week at No. 1
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's music update. We're taking a look at the latest from the UK charts, and it's all about the comeback kings and queens.
[Music transitions]
Host: Michael Jackson is still on top, with "The Essential Michael Jackson" spending its second week at number one on the Official Albums Chart. This renewed interest in the King of Pop's music is thanks in part to the recent biopic, which has fueled strong streaming and physical sales. In fact, "The Essential" returned to number one for the first time in 17 years just last week.
[Music transitions]
Host: But Michael Jackson isn't the only one making waves. Westlife's new compilation, "25 – The Ultimate Collection", debuts at number two, becoming the Irish boyband's 15th top 10 LP in the UK. And Noah Kahan's "The Great Divide" rises to number three.
[Music transitions]
Host: Olivia Dean's "The Art of Loving" follows at number four, and Michael Jackson's classic "Thriller" climbs to number five. We're also seeing some new entries in the top 10, like Reverend and The Makers' "Is This How Happiness Feels?" at number seven.
[Music transitions]
Host: And in other news, Harry Styles' "Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally." soars back into the chart at number nine, just in time for his upcoming tour. Katy Perry's compilation "The One That Got the Plays" comes in at number 13, and Billie Eilish's "Hit Me Hard and Soft" returns to the top 40 at number 32.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for this week's music update. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you next time.
